• Commercialisation Strategy: Exploring partnerships with pharmaceutical manufacturers, testing laboratories, distributors and technology companies for potential pilot evaluations.

TD POWER SYSTEMS Q2 FY27: REVENUE SURGES 86% YOY, EBITDA JUMPS 102%, PAT MORE THAN DOUBLES; ₹2,319 CR ORDER BOOK, ₹824 CR NEW ORDERS & STRONG EXPORT DEMAND FROM DATA CENTRES, GAS TURBINES AND HYDROPOWER

• Revenue: Increased 85.9% YoY to ₹841.32 Cr, supported by strong domestic and export execution.

• Order Book: Strong outstanding orders of ₹2,318.7 Cr as of September 2026, with approximately 74% from exports.

• New Orders: Q2 order inflows increased 57% YoY to approximately ₹824 Cr, with exports contributing 88%.

• H1 FY27 Performance: Revenue grew approximately 80% YoY to ₹1,481.37 Cr; EBITDA surged 89% to ₹295.37 Cr and PAT rose 90% to ₹210.04 Cr.

• H1 Order Inflows: Increased 70% YoY to ₹1,558.5 Cr, with exports accounting for 90% of orders.

• Gas Engine Generators: Secured large-volume orders from global OEMs for data-centre and distributed-power applications, including repeat orders from the Americas.

• Gas Turbine Business: Won significant orders from two major global OEMs, supported by demand from data centres, oil & gas and industrial power generation.

• Hydropower Business: Secured its largest vertical hydro-generator order for a Nepal project, along with horizontal hydro-generator orders.

• Steam Turbine Generators: Won a major 60 MW steel-industry order and a 4 × 16 MW order for a barge-mounted power plant.

• International Expansion: Global installed base reached 8,772 units across 114 countries, with Mongolia added as a new market.

• Hydro Business Outlook: Management expects recovery in hydro-generator demand over the coming quarters, supported by a healthy enquiry pipeline across South Asia, Europe and India.

• Management Outlook: Positive on export-led growth, global OEM partnerships, data-centre power demand, gas turbine opportunities and hydropower recovery, supported by strong order inflows and manufacturing capabilities.

Singapore stressed Huang was not investigated for espionage.

Investigations into Megaspeed and six other individuals remain ongoing.

Singapore also accused US server supplier Supermicro of limited cooperation with investigators.

VODAFONE IDEA Q2 FY27: REVENUE UP 6.2% YOY, CASH EBITDA RISES 11.2%; ₹5,975 CR NET LOSS, ₹10,500+ CR FUNDING SECURED, 5G EXPANDS TO 400 CITIES & ARPU REACHES ₹198

• Cash EBITDA: Rose 11.2% YoY to ₹2,498 Cr, while reported EBITDA increased 6.3% YoY to ₹4,981 Cr.

• Net Loss: Reported loss of ₹5,975 Cr, impacted by adverse mark-to-market valuation of treasury assets.

• Adjusted Loss: Reduced to ₹5,513 Cr from ₹5,562 Cr YoY, excluding exceptional items.

• Capital Expenditure: Q2 capex reached ₹3,946 Cr, with orders worth over ₹13,200 Cr placed under the three-year capex programme.

• Funding: Secured over ₹10,500 Cr in funding and facilities during H1 FY27, including over ₹4,000 Cr incremental bank funding in Q2.

• Cash & Debt: Cash and bank balance stood at ₹5,470 Cr, while bank debt was ₹943 Cr as of September 2026.

• 5G Expansion: Extended 5G coverage to 400 cities and towns across 17 key telecom circles.

• 4G Network Expansion: Added over 22,500 broadband towers in 12 months, including nearly 9,000 during Q2.

• 4G Coverage: Population coverage reached approximately 88%, with plans to increase coverage beyond 95% across 17 key circles.

• ARPU Growth: Increased 9.7% YoY to ₹198 from ₹180, supported by customer upgrades.

• Subscriber Base: Total subscribers increased to 194.4 million from 193.1 million QoQ.

• 4G/5G Subscribers: Increased to 131 million from 127.8 million YoY.

• Data Consumption: Rose 27.1% YoY to 93.6 PB per day.

• Enterprise Business: Announced strategic partnership with Hindalco to deploy a dedicated private network at its Baphlimali bauxite mine.

• Management Outlook: Focused on accelerating 4G/5G network expansion, improving customer experience, increasing ARPU and strengthening network competitiveness through sustained capex and funding support.

SAI URJA: Declared L1 bidder for an ₹8.84 Cr NTPC order covering the complete control and instrumentation system at NTPC Sipat Super Thermal Power Station, with a two-year execution period.

PRARUH: Wins a DMRC contract for telecom network infrastructure upgradation across Line 1, 2 and 3 Phase-I stations, including PRC system upgradation at OCC MB and BCC SHPK; the supplied headline and detailed disclosure mention different order values, so the value requires verification. Execution period is six months.

📍 ACQUISITION

ECLERX: Wholly owned US subsidiary eClerx LLC signs an agreement to acquire 100% of RegEdge LLC for consideration of up to $12 million, including performance-linked earnouts; the US-based regulatory consulting firm reported CY25 revenue of $5.1 million, strengthening eClerx's financial services compliance capabilities.

📍 COLLABORATION

ADANIENT: Subsidiary Kutch Copper signs an MoU with Chile's Codelco for strategic exploration at the Kaburkaala copper project, linking Chilean copper resources with Adani's Mundra smelter and supporting long-term raw material security.

HEGAM: Subsidiary TACC signs a non-binding MoU with a global lithium-ion cell manufacturer for potential supply of up to 40,000 tonnes of synthetic graphite-based anode active material, alongside R&D for next-generation battery materials.

RAJNISH WELLNESS: Enters into a strategic distribution association with JNTL Consumer Health India for the Kalyan–Thane region, covering Baby Care, Skin Care, Oral Care, Feminine Hygiene and Cold/Cough/Allergy products.

CUBICAL FINANCIAL: Signs a non-binding MoU with Consider Done EV Mobility LLP to finance e-rickshaws through its dealer and distributor network; no financial commitment or deal value has been disclosed.

EMERALD FINANCE: Enters into a pan-India Direct Selling Agent agreement with Utkarsh Small Finance Bank to source gold loan business, expanding its distribution operations through a new fee-based channel.

📍 LEADERSHIP CHANGES

5PAISA: Appoints Devi Yesodharan as Chief Content and Research Officer and Senior Management Personnel, effective November 13, 2026; she brings over 21 years of experience, including a previous role as CMO of Trendlyne.

📍 NEW PROJECTS

ORIENT GREEN POWER: Commissions a 17.6 MW solar plant, taking total solar capacity to 24.6 MW, and signs an EPC contract for an additional 6.6 MW wind project; 7.8 MW wind repowering is nearing completion, subject to regulatory approvals.

MAN INDUSTRIES: Plans a $110 million investment through its wholly owned US subsidiary to establish a 3,50,000 MTPA HSAW pipe manufacturing facility, targeting demand in the US and international markets, subject to regulatory approvals.

RAMAPHO: Commences trial production of Single Super Phosphate (SSP) fertiliser under Phase-I of its greenfield Nardana plant in Maharashtra, with commercial production expected after receiving statutory approvals.

NAVA: Commissions a 100 MW solar power project in Zambia and advances its 300 MW MEL Phase-II power expansion, targeted for full commissioning by July 2027.

• Capex Timeline: Majority of ongoing capacity expansion projects expected to be completed by 2028.

• Growth Opportunities: Renewable energy integration, battery storage, data centres, semiconductors and high-voltage transmission infrastructure remain key growth drivers.

• Management Outlook: Focused on converting its strong order backlog into revenue, improving margins through productivity and operational efficiency, and expanding exports, services and manufacturing capacity.

📊 JEFFERIES INDIA STRATEGY | ABHINAV SINHA

FPI FLOWS – POTENTIAL REVIVAL BENEFICIARIES

• FPI Flows – After persistent selling, foreign portfolio investor flows have recently turned positive.

• Key Triggers – Potential AI-trade reversal, equity tax relief, resilient domestic macro, reasonable large-cap valuations and light positioning could sustain inflows.

• Large-Cap Focus – Large caps could be the cleaner play on a revival in FPI flows.

• Valuations – Large-cap valuations have become more reasonable.

• Key Rationale – Higher liquidity and greater FPI ownership make large caps more direct beneficiaries of returning foreign flows.

CITI on Bharti Airtel ; Buy, TP Rs 2390

In a notable reversal, Bharti has reinstated its Rs299 recharge plan 3 months after withdrawing it in Aug'26.

While earlier plan offered 1.5 GB/day of data, relaunched version provides 1 GB/day.

Move reflects Bharti's response to competitive pressures, as peers did not follow its earlier tariff action, as well as elevated churn during 2Q.

Churn increased from 2.6% to 2.9% qoq, resulting in net subscriber additions slowing sharply qoq from +3.3m to +0.7m

Decision underscores challenges of implementing unilateral tariff actions in prepaid smartphone segment, where competitive intensity remains highest

It suggests that pricing discipline is difficult to sustain without broader industry participation.

Note that based on certain assumptions around Bharti's subscriber mix, had estimated the Aug'26 move could potentially benefit ARPU by c.Rs4/mth (EPS benefit of c.2%).

Bharti recently reported ARPU improvement from Rs264 to Rs271 in 2Q.

• Q2 consolidated EBITDA rose 42% YoY but declined 8% QoQ.

• India upstream EBITDA stood at ₹7,000 Cr, downstream at ₹330 Cr, copper at ₹1,670 Cr and Novelis at ₹4,860 Cr.

• Novelis insurance recovery reached $1.3 BN, including $900 MN already received.

• India costs expected to rise further in Q3; benefits from expansion projects remain back-ended.

• Citi sees limited upside in LME aluminium prices from current levels.

GOLDMAN SACHS ON TATA STEEL ; MAINTAINS NEUTRAL, TARGET PRICE ₹215 (CMP ₹190.20)

• Domestic operations remain highly efficient, while European operations continue to face uncertainty.

• India steel realisations expected to rise ₹3,500/tonne QoQ, offsetting higher coking coal costs.

• FY27 European cost savings could face challenges due to lower production volumes.

• Net Debt/EBITDA at 2.4x remains within management's 2.5x guidance.

• Domestic profitability expected to increasingly depend on downstream product mix until NINL capacity expansion by FY30.

CLSA ON ONGC ; HIGH CONVICTION OUTPERFORM, TARGET PRICE ₹405 (CMP ₹234.80)

• Q2 standalone net profit missed estimates by 5% due to impairment losses and a one-off provision.

• EBITDA and core PBT beat estimates by 7% and 4%, respectively.

• Declared interim dividend of ₹8/share, implying a 3.5% dividend yield.

• KG-98/2 and Daman projects expected to drive production volume growth in FY27–28.

• CLSA sees 76% upside potential based on its assumption of Brent crude at $82/barrel in FY28.

CITI ON GLAND PHARMA ; MAINTAINS SELL, TARGET PRICE ₹2,360 (CMP ₹3,132.80)

• Citi believes current valuations already factor in significant growth and margin improvement.

GOLDMAN SACHS ON VOLTAS ; MAINTAINS SELL, TARGET PRICE ₹1,025 (CMP ₹1,056.50)

• UCP segment delivered strong volume growth, gaining market share in room ACs and Voltas Beko (Voltbek).

• UCP margin recovery remained below expectations despite strong volume growth.

• EMPS margins benefited from a one-off write-back, while the engineering business remained strong.

• October price hikes expected to support UCP margin improvement from Q4.

• TARGET IMPLIES 2.98% DOWNSIDE from the quoted CMP.

Despite low local compute demand, India's low construction and power costs attract global operators, though hosting foreign compute raises geopolitical neutrality questions.

Curious when FII will come back to India

So gave Co-pilot a prompt
“Why FIIs wont return to India even as AI trade unwind globally”

Reverse Psychology

Here is the response

1. India is still expensive vs EM peers
o Even after corrections, India trades at a premium to most emerging markets.
o FIIs compare India with China, Korea, Taiwan, Brazil, not with India's own history.
o If China is at 10-12x PE and India at 20-25x PE, capital tends to chase cheaper markets. 
2. India lacks direct AI beneficiaries
o The AI trade created winners in US tech, Taiwan semiconductors and Korean memory-chip companies.
o India has very few large listed AI, semiconductor or hyperscaler plays that global thematic funds can buy. 
3. Dollar returns matter, not rupee returns
o FIIs think in USD.
o Even if Nifty is flat or slightly up, rupee depreciation can wipe out returns.
o Currency risk remains a major deterrent for foreign capital. 
4. US yields remain a strong competitor
o If US Treasuries offer attractive risk-free returns, FIIs need a much higher expected return from India.
o Many global allocators prefer earning 4-5% in dollar assets rather than taking EM risk. 
5. India's earnings growth has moderated
o India's premium valuation was justified when earnings were compounding rapidly.
o If earnings growth slows while valuations remain rich, FIIs question the risk-reward. 
6. Better opportunities elsewhere
o Korea, Taiwan and China offer exposure to AI, semiconductors and manufacturing at lower valuations.
o Global funds have finite capital; India is competing against these markets for allocation. 
7. India is no longer an under-owned market
o After years of strong inflows, most EM funds already have meaningful India exposure.
o Incremental flows require a new catalyst, not just the absence of AI enthusiasm.
8. Domestic flows reduce urgency
o SIPs, mutual funds and insurance money continue supporting Indian markets despite FII selling.
o Paradoxically, this resilience prevents large valuation corrections that would otherwise attract FIIs back.

Maruti Suzuki India should be rechristened as Suzuki India

Maruti's journey started as a Govt of India project. Maruti Udyog was the Indian promoter & Suzuki was brought in as the technology partner. Back then, this was very much an Indian company with Japanese know-how.

Over time, the Indian promoter gradually diluted its holding & eventually exited completely. Suzuki did the opposite, staying invested through every cycle & steadily increasing its stake.

What began as a JV slowly became Suzuki's most important global asset. The ownership story itself tells you who has deepened commitment over the decades.

For years, investors debated why Suzuki was setting up fresh manufacturing capacity outside Maruti Suzuki through its Gujarat subsidiary instead of housing it directly in the listed entity.

Then came the reversal. Suzuki transferred Suzuki Motor Gujarat into Maruti Suzuki at a valuation of roughly ₹12,000+ Cr. Rather than taking cash, it largely took equity.

The result? Suzuki's ownership in Maruti Suzuki moved up further without having to buy equivalent shares from the secondary market.

This wasn't just a restructuring exercise. It was Suzuki effectively converting manufacturing assets into a larger stake in India's largest PV company.

Even after that transaction, Suzuki did not stop. It has periodically picked up additional shares from the open market whenever opportunities emerged.

The message is clear. The Indian promoter exited long ago. The Japanese promoter keeps doubling down on India.

Look at the cars on the road today. The branding emphasis is on the giant "S" logo. 10-15years back, cars started selling with only “S” logo, 1st on premium nexa cars, then on all the models. You will hardly see Maruti branded cars on road now

For many younger buyers, the brand recall is shifting from "Maruti Suzuki" to simply "Suzuki". The transition is subtle but visible.

India is now the crown jewel of Suzuki Motor Corp. A substantial portion of Suzuki valuation come from Indian listed entity. Maruti $38bn mcap translate to $21bn (for 58% stake, $15bn if applied 30% Holdco disc).

Even beyond that, Maruti pays over $500m to Suzuki as royalty, that value must be over $5bn in the SoTP of Suzuki motors. Suzuki motors also have successful 2w biz in India, they are 6th largest 2w in India, clocking over 1lac units every month

In many ways, investors buying Suzuki Motor Corp are indirectly buying the India story. Cars sold by Suzuki in India is higher than overall car sold by Suzuki in other 100 countries combined

A rebranding to "Suzuki India" could also help shed the old "cheap small-car company" perception. As premium SUVs, hybrids & future EVs gain share, a stronger global MNC identity may command a different customer mindset.

Ownership, capital allocation, manufacturing integration, branding & growth strategy all point in one direction: this is increasingly Suzuki's India story.

Conclusion: Maruti only stays in Co. name hence should be renamed now
